title: Shopify Theme Design Principles — Merchant Experience
content: Official Shopify theme design principles for merchant experience (from shopify.dev). These govern how themes should be built and directly inform Figma design decisions. PURPOSEFUL: Design sections and blocks tailored to target audience. Create different sections for each template to showcase different customer experiences. Define segments based on target audience, inventory size, and customer experience. Build opinionated theme art direction aligned with ecommerce best practices. Build variations of the same component rather than providing two components that achieve the same purpose. EASY TO SET UP: Keep theme settings to the minimum required to empower the majority of merchants. Avoid niche settings and edge-case configurations. Use blocks to improve section usability and facilitate content reordering. Create theme empty states and placeholders that leverage existing store data. ANTIFRAGILE: Components must function professionally without perfect assets or image ratios. Use atomic design approach to theme components. Maintain robust layouts regardless of content volume or missing data. Implement scalable font hierarchies across different scenarios. Make sure font styles are associated with the right elements (all headings with same font setting). Apply colour systems consistently for optimal contrast and accessibility. Prevent critical actions from being obscured by floating app components. FLEXIBLE: All flexibility provided in the theme must be predictable. Provide settings aligned with SEO, accessibility, layout responsiveness, content management, and localisation best practices. Avoid replacing platform functionality with theme settings. Avoid workarounds beyond displaying and organising content. EXTENSIBLE: Support metafields, theme blocks, and app blocks. Add support for app blocks in sections that have clear use cases for layering additional conversion tools or purchase decision factors. FIGMA IMPLICATION: When designing Shopify themes in Figma, every section frame should work with placeholder content, missing images, and variable text lengths. Design empty states for every section. Build component variants rather than separate components for similar purposes.

title: Shopify Theme Design Principles — Customer Experience
content: Official Shopify customer experience design principles (from shopify.dev). These define what a well-designed Shopify storefront must deliver. ACCESSIBLE: Required standard for Shopify theme store submission. Apply colour system best practices for robust colour palettes. Design components that respect DOM order and element tab order. Reference Polaris accessibility considerations for component design. EXPRESSIVE: Enable merchant storytelling through dedicated sections. Include sections for lifestyle imagery, video, and text content. Display compelling layouts that communicate merchant identity and differentiation. INTUITIVE: Tailor product discovery experience to target segment. Design prominent and discoverable navigation with intuitive menu interactions. Include entry points such as featured collection or highlighted products section. Design each product page with prominent title, price, and buy button. Make sure description and secondary information are easily discoverable. Select design patterns that build trust with customers. Test theme with real users including decision-making scenarios. COHESIVE: Ensure consistent scale, spacing, component weight, layouts, and page design across the entire store. EFFICIENT: Limit the number of steps required to make a purchase. Enable accelerated checkout by default. Design navigation and interaction patterns with immediate feedback that feels performant. Optimise layouts for a powerful mobile-first experience. Avoid elements that require additional cognitive load to understand. KEY PREREQUISITES: Establish feedback loop between theme designer and developer. Theme should not sacrifice performance at the expense of design. FIGMA IMPLICATION: When building Shopify storefronts in Figma, ensure every page has clear visual hierarchy with title, price, and buy button as the dominant elements. Navigation must be tested at all breakpoints. Accelerated checkout buttons (Shop Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay) must be included by default in product page and cart designs.

title: Shopify Subscription UX — Product Form Components
content: Official Shopify subscription UX guidelines for product forms (from shopify.dev). The product form for subscriptions has four subcomponents: Price, Selling Plan Selection, Selling Plan Details, and Main CTA. PRICE SUBCOMPONENT: Display selling_plan_allocation.price reflecting the selected subscription. Show compare_at_price when applicable. Display per_delivery_price only when different from price (prepaid subscriptions). Show unit_price when relevant (unit measurement varies by sellingPlanAllocations). Subscription badge: display when selling plan involves recurring deliveries. Do NOT display badge when item can only be purchased as subscription — use alternative methods. Price adjustment messaging examples: 'Subscription - Save $3.00', 'Subscription - Save 10%', for changing pricing: 'Save up to 30%'. TWO PRICING PATTERNS: (1) Main Price Component — single price on page updated via selling plan/variant selection. Clearly display subscription price and savings vs one-time purchase. Add subscription badge to clarify savings condition. Best when app controls both theme codebase sections. (2) Inline Pricing — price displays near selling plan selection, updates based on plan and variant changes. Makes strong association between plan choice and price. Preferred for mobile (smaller screens keep price in view). Useful for subscription apps integrating into third-party themes. Avoids conflicts because pricing is contained within app-controlled selling plan selector. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design both pricing patterns as component variants. For inline pricing, ensure the price label sits directly adjacent to the selling plan radio/dropdown. On mobile, inline pricing is preferred — price must remain visible without scrolling when selecting a plan.

title: Shopify Subscription UX — Selling Plan Selection & Options
content: Official Shopify selling plan selection UX guidelines (from shopify.dev). SELLING PLAN SELECTION SUBCOMPONENT: Use the term 'subscriptions' in designs. Treat subscriptions and one-time purchase as separate groups. Default behaviour: on first page load, select one-time purchase by default. When customer interacts, collapse the unselected group. Disable selling plan group selection when unavailable for a given variant. LABEL DISPLAY RULES: Show 'Subscriptions' label when one-time purchase exists AND at least one sellingPlanGroup is present, OR when one-time purchase is unavailable but multiple sellingPlanGroups of different types exist. Do NOT show label when no selling plan groups exist, or when product is subscription-only with single selling plan group (use group name without radio input instead). GROUP LAYOUT: Prioritise vertically stacked list — avoid side-by-side on smaller screens (causes crowding on mobile). Display as radio inputs instead of buttons — buttons compete with the product form's main CTA. GROUP NAME: Selling plan names should make clear the benefit (e.g. 'Subscribe and save 10%'). Differentiates multiple selling plan groups on a single product. OPTION VALUE DISPLAY: Show all option values at a glance from a group. 4 options or fewer: radio buttons. More than 4: select dropdown. Apply same layout to all values in a group for consistency. Never express exact prices in option values (currency-dependent) — percentages are acceptable. VARIANT CHANGE HANDLING: When selected option becomes unavailable after variant change: (1) unselect unavailable options, (2) disable unavailable options for selected variant, (3) keep form submission button enabled — do not disable it, (4) on error: anchor/scroll to UI area and show message describing issue and resolution steps. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design selling plan selectors as radio groups, not buttons. Always show the collapsed state as a variant. Design the error state with inline message anchored to the selector, not a toast or modal. Test at mobile width to ensure vertical stacking works.

title: Shopify Subscription UX — Details, Cart, Orders & Multi-Currency
content: Official Shopify subscription UX for selling plan details, cart, orders, and currency handling (from shopify.dev). SELLING PLAN DETAILS: Express the number of payment cycles at current price and communicate future price changes. Examples: 'first payment $6.00, then $9.00', 'first 3 payments $7.00 each, then $9.00', 'first payment free, then $9.00'. Description field may contain promotional text, cancellation policies, refund info. Do NOT express exact prices in description — use percentages. Include link to subscription policy (shop.subscription_policy, links to /policies/subscription-policy). TRANSPARENCY RULE: If initial price incentive is applied, explain current payment AND how payments change in future. Lack of information causes customer mistrust and may appear misleading. Certain states/countries have laws around price clarity — merchants may be subject to lawsuits. MAIN CTA: When product requires selling plan or one is selected, switch CTA text to subscription-specific label (e.g. 'Add subscription to cart'). Helps customers differentiate between subscription and one-time purchase. CART ITEMS: Display selling_plan.name in cart line items — do NOT list individual option values alongside the name. The selling plan name is meant to accurately summarise the subscription. Same text appears at checkout and order details. SELLING PLAN NAME RULES: Must be succinct, easily understood by customers. Should NOT be marketing text. State delivery frequency and prepaid period if applicable. Do NOT state exact dollar amounts (e.g. '$9 a month') — use percentages. Shopify does not control the name value — merchants can enter any text via an app. MULTI-CURRENCY: Merchants can sell in multiple currencies. Shopify offers currency selector and price rounding. CRITICAL: Apps and merchants must NOT write any prices in text strings shown to customers — they won't reflect currency switching or rounding and may be incorrect or misleading. Price properties from Liquid/JSON APIs reflect the customer's session currency and rounding rules. Use percentages whenever possible (e.g. 'Deliver every week (Save 20%)'). ORDER DETAILS: Show selling_plan.name in order line items. Customers logged in can view past orders — important to let them easily identify subscription products. MULTI-LOCATION: Surface subscription savings and pricing on product pages, collection pages, search results, featured product sections, and quick view modals. FIGMA IMPLICATION: When designing cart line items, always include selling plan name as a secondary line below product title. Design the subscription policy link as an inline text link within the selling plan details area. Never hard-code prices in Figma text layers for subscription components — use placeholder tokens that indicate dynamic values.

title: Shopify Pre-order & TBYB UX — Product Form Components
content: Official Shopify pre-order and try-before-you-buy UX guidelines for product forms (from shopify.dev). A pre-order or TBYB is any transaction where payment or fulfilment does not happen at time of purchase. CLARITY REQUIREMENTS: Customers must clearly identify options and make a choice (e.g. 'try now, pay later'). Customers must clearly identify: how much they pay at checkout, total product cost, when remaining balance is charged (if applicable), and when payment method is charged. Merchants must provide exact dates, ranges, or trial duration estimates. UI must integrate seamlessly into existing theme design. Use language customers understand that refers to actual purchase terms: 'pre-order', 'back-order', 'TBYB'. DISPLAY LOCATIONS: Products with alternative purchasing options appear on product pages, collection pages, search results, featured product sections on home pages, and quick view modals on product cards. PRICE COMPONENT: Display full product price. Include contextual pre-order/TBYB badge or label. CRITICAL: Do NOT use visual styling that suggests money-saving pricing tactics (such as price strikethroughs) to represent full price in relation to initial deposit. Display full price clearly; show deposit separately if required. SELLING PLAN SELECTION: Same rules as subscription selection — show 'Purchase options' label when one-time purchase AND sellingPlanGroup exist, or when multiple groups of different types exist. Do NOT show label when no groups exist or product is single-group only (use group name without radio). Default to one-time on first load. Collapse unselected groups. Disable unavailable groups per variant. Vertically stacked list preferred. Radio inputs preferred over buttons. Do NOT express exact prices in option values (e.g. '$50 deposit') — use percentages. 4 or fewer options: radio buttons. More than 4: select dropdown. VARIANT CHANGE: Unselect unavailable options, disable them, keep submit button enabled. On error: anchor to problem area with descriptive message. SELLING PLAN DETAILS: Do NOT express exact prices in descriptions. Include links to returns or billing policies. MAIN CTA: Switch to purchase-option-specific text when selling plan is selected. Use accelerated checkout button label for deferred purchase options. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design pre-order and TBYB as distinct badge variants on the price component. Never use strikethrough styling for deposit vs full price — design a clear two-line layout showing 'Full price: $X' and 'Due at checkout: $Y' as separate text elements. Design the CTA with at least three label variants: 'Add to cart' (one-time), 'Pre-order now', and 'Try before you buy'.

title: Shopify Pre-order & TBYB UX — Cart, Orders & Naming
content: Official Shopify pre-order and TBYB UX for cart, orders, and naming conventions (from shopify.dev). CART PAGE: Customers scan cart before proceeding to checkout — all elements must be clearly represented. Required elements: (1) Selling plan name (selling_plan.name) — do NOT list individual option values alongside the name. (2) Full product price — remind customer of total cost. (3) Price at checkout (selling_plan.checkout_charge.value) — for pre-order this is usually the deposit amount; for TBYB this is usually $0 indicating no payment required at checkout. CART NOTIFICATION: Show selling plan name and full product price. Same rule: do not list individual option values alongside selling plan name. SELLING PLAN NAME RULES: Must be succinct, easily understood. Should NOT include marketing text. State the type of deferred purchase option. Write deposit amount and payment due date for customer reference throughout purchase journey. Shopify does not control the name value — merchants can enter any text via an app. MULTI-CURRENCY: Same rules as subscriptions — never write prices in text strings. Prices in strings won't reflect currency switching or rounding and may be incorrect or misleading. Price properties from Liquid/JSON APIs reflect customer session currency and rounding rules. ORDER DETAILS: Show selling_plan.name (not individual option values), full product price, and price at checkout. Important to let customer easily identify pre-order or TBYB products in order history. KEY TERMINOLOGY: Pre-order = product purchased before available. TBYB = trial purchase model. Deferred payment/fulfilment = transaction not completed at point of purchase. Selling plan = structured purchase option with specific terms. Selling plan group = category of related selling plans. Selling plan allocation = association of product variant with specific selling plan. Checkout charge = amount due at time of purchase. Deposit = initial payment portion in pre-order models. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Cart line items for pre-order/TBYB need three text lines: product name, selling plan name, and checkout charge. Design a clear visual distinction between 'Total price' and 'Due at checkout' — use different font weights or a subtle background to separate them. For TBYB, design the $0 checkout state with clear 'No charge today' messaging, not just '$0.00'.
